milestones.title: Sprint 1
milestones.description: Picked in Sprint 1 planning. Set the due date to the sprint's last day.

epic.title: Epic 1: Audio & AI pipeline (local)
epic.body:
**Goal:** Turn lecture audio into German text live on the THA GPU server, without any data leaving campus.

**Starting point:** Hajar's first test in [`research/asr-benchmark/`](https://github.com/Campus-Caption/CampusCaption/tree/main/research/asr-benchmark): `small` ~31% WER, `large-v3-turbo` ~14% on a 30 s lecture-style text. Biggest problems: English terms (PyTorch → Python) and wrong numbers (15. → 12. Dezember).

**Done when**
- [ ] The model runs fully locally, nothing is sent outside
- [ ] Silero VAD filters silence, no invented text on silent audio
- [ ] WER and CER are measured on our own consented lecture recordings, results in `research/`
- [ ] End-to-end delay (speech → text on screen) is measured; team agrees on a target (suggestion: ≤ 4 s)

issues.title: Compare the German Whisper fine-tune with large-v3-turbo
issues.body:
Run `primeline/whisper-large-v3-turbo-german` on the same test text as Hajar's first test and compare with `large-v3-turbo`.

**Done when**
- [ ] Table with WER, CER and serious errors for both models, added to `research/asr-benchmark/README.md`
- [ ] Short decision record in `docs/decisions/` on which model we use

issues.title: Test term hints for technical words
issues.body:
Give Whisper a list of course terms (PyTorch, Machine Learning, Backpropagation …) via `initial_prompt` or `hotwords` in faster-whisper and check whether those errors disappear.

**Done when**
- [ ] Before/after comparison on the test text
- [ ] Note on whether hints cause new errors (e.g. the model writing a hint word that wasn't said)

issues.title: Add Silero VAD and a hallucination blocklist
issues.body:
Put Silero VAD in front of Whisper so only speech reaches the model. Add a small blocklist of phrases Whisper invents on silence in German (e.g. "Untertitelung des ZDF für funk, 2017").

**Done when**
- [ ] 60 s of silence or room noise produces no text
- [ ] Blocklist lives in one file that's easy to extend

issues.title: Pick a live streaming method and measure the delay
issues.body:
Whisper isn't built for live audio. Test a streaming wrapper (SimulStreaming, WhisperLiveKit or whisper_streaming) with German speech.

**Done when**
- [ ] Delay from spoken word to text measured (median and worst case)
- [ ] WER in streaming mode compared to file mode
- [ ] Decision record on which wrapper we use

issues.title: Record at least 5–6 hours of consented lecture audio
issues.body:
We need real lecture audio to test on, not only read test texts. Aim for at least 6 speakers, different accents and subjects, and both lav mic and the hall system if possible.

**Blocked by:** the consent form (Epic 4).

**Done when**
- [ ] At least 5–6 h recorded with written consent
- [ ] Reference transcripts for at least a part of it
- [ ] Files stored in the agreed private folder, **never in Git** (decision 0002)

issues.title: Get access to a THA GPU server
issues.body:
Ask Zentrale IT for a machine with a GPU (at least 10 GB VRAM) that we can run the model on.

**Done when**
- [ ] We know which machine, how we log in, and what we're allowed to install
- [ ] One team member has run `large-v3-turbo` on it

issues.title: Rate caption errors by how serious they are
issues.body:
WER counts every error the same. Rate errors as minor (0.25), standard (0.5) or serious (1.0), like Hajar's step 2 part B, so we can see which errors actually mislead students.

**Done when**
- [ ] A simple rating sheet or script
- [ ] Rating done for the chosen model on the test set

epic.title: Epic 2: Backend & local infrastructure
epic.body:
**Goal:** One FastAPI service on the campus network that takes audio in and sends captions to many screens at once.

**Done when**
- [ ] Audio stays in a RAM buffer of max 30 s and never touches the disk ([decision 0002](https://github.com/Campus-Caption/CampusCaption/blob/main/docs/decisions/0002-no-audio-on-disk.md)), checked by a test
- [ ] WebSockets send the captions to many connected screens at the same time
- [ ] Runs with `docker compose up` on the campus network without any cloud service

issues.title: WebSocket rooms: one lecturer, many viewers
issues.body:
A lecturer starts a room, viewers join with a room code, and every caption is sent to everyone in that room.

**Done when**
- [ ] Two rooms can run at the same time without mixing captions
- [ ] A viewer that reconnects gets the latest captions again

issues.title: Agree the caption message format with the frontend
issues.body:
Write down what a caption message looks like (text, interim/final, timestamp, speaker label later) and the WebSocket endpoints. FastAPI's automatic `/docs` page covers the HTTP part for free.

**Done when**
- [ ] One short file in `docs/` that frontend and backend both agreed on

issues.title: Take audio from a mic or the hall system into the server
issues.body:
Read audio from a USB mic or the lecture hall audio output (e.g. with `sounddevice`), convert to 16 kHz mono and keep it in a RAM ring buffer of max 30 s.

**Done when**
- [ ] Works with at least one real mic
- [ ] Buffer never grows beyond 30 s

issues.title: Automatic check that no audio is written to disk
issues.body:
A test that runs the pipeline and then checks that no audio ended up in logs, temp folders or Docker volumes.

**Done when**
- [ ] Test is in the repo and runs before every merge (or at least before every demo)

issues.title: Decide whether we need a database in v1
issues.body:
If students join without accounts and we don't store transcripts, v1 may not need a database at all. Decide before building one.

**Done when**
- [ ] Decision record: no database yet, or Postgres with what tables and why

issues.title: Protect the lecturer control page
issues.body:
Only the lecturer may start, pause and end captions. A simple shared secret is enough for the prototype ([decision 0003](https://github.com/Campus-Caption/CampusCaption/blob/main/docs/decisions/0003-no-student-login-in-v1.md)).

**Done when**
- [ ] Control endpoints reject requests without the secret

issues.title: Check if we need local HTTPS (campuscaption.local)
issues.body:
Browsers only allow the microphone on HTTPS pages. If audio comes from a mic plugged into the server, viewers don't need HTTPS for that. Check our setup first, then set up Caddy/Nginx only if needed.

**Done when**
- [ ] Decision written down; HTTPS set up if we need it

issues.title: Load test: how many viewers can one server handle
issues.body:
Simulate many viewers in one or more rooms.

**Done when**
- [ ] Number of viewers and rooms one server handles, and on what hardware

epic.title: Epic 3: UX & frontend
epic.body:
**Goal:** A caption viewer for students and a control panel for lecturers. Laptop first, then phone and projector.

**Starting point:** Simge's UX research (hybrid viewer: 2–3 live lines plus an optional history panel, UX-01 to UX-06) and the student survey (laptop/tablet 77%, phone and projector 38% each, 38% worried about distraction).

**Done when**
- [ ] Works on laptop, phone and projector
- [ ] Meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and works with the keyboard
- [ ] Feedback collected from hard-of-hearing students / the disabled students' representative

issues.title: Pick the frontend stack
issues.body:
Vue, React or plain HTML/CSS/JS. Pick what the frontend people are fastest with; the viewer is a small app.

**Done when**
- [ ] Short decision record in `docs/decisions/`

issues.title: Rough wireframes: viewer, lecturer panel, join screen
issues.body:
Paper, Penpot or Figma, whatever is fastest. The point is to agree on what the screens contain, not pixel-perfect design.

**Done when**
- [ ] Wireframes for the three screens, phone and laptop size, linked or added under `docs/`
- [ ] Team looked at them in a sprint review

issues.title: Build the caption viewer
issues.body:
Hybrid viewer from the UX research: 2–3 live lines, collapsible history, "Jump to Live" when scrolled up, interim text grey and italic, final text solid (UX-01, UX-04, UX-05).

**Done when**
- [ ] Shows live captions from the backend
- [ ] Scrolling up pauses auto-scroll; Jump to Live brings it back

issues.title: Text size presets and light/dark theme
issues.body:
Small 20 px, Medium 24 px, Large 28 px, XL 32 px, and a light and dark theme (UX-02, UX-03).

**Done when**
- [ ] Settings change instantly and the layout doesn't break
- [ ] All colour pairs checked for WCAG AA contrast

issues.title: Join a room by room code or QR code
issues.body:
Students open a link or scan a QR code on the projector. No login ([decision 0003](https://github.com/Campus-Caption/CampusCaption/blob/main/docs/decisions/0003-no-student-login-in-v1.md)).

**Done when**
- [ ] QR code shown on the lecturer panel / projector view
- [ ] Joining takes one tap on a phone

issues.title: Lecturer panel: start, pause, end
issues.body:
Simple control page for the lecturer, with a clear "Live" state.

**Done when**
- [ ] Start, pause and end work and viewers see the state change

issues.title: Status badge and privacy notice in the viewer
issues.body:
Show Live / Reconnecting / Offline, and a short privacy notice that only says what the backend really does (UX-06).

**Done when**
- [ ] Status changes are announced to screen readers
- [ ] Privacy text agreed with Epic 4

issues.title: Usability test with hard-of-hearing students
issues.body:
Test the prototype with hard-of-hearing students and the disabled students' representative.

**Done when**
- [ ] At least 3 sessions done, findings written down as new issues

epic.title: Epic 4: Privacy, ethics & GDPR
epic.body:
**Goal:** Make sure the system follows GDPR, §201 StGB and BayDSG, and get the approvals we need before testing in lectures.

**Done when**
- [ ] Written testing approval from the data protection officer
- [ ] Consent forms ready for students and lecturers
- [ ] "Live-Untertitelung aktiv (KI)" signs designed and ready for lecture halls

issues.title: Discuss the RAM-buffer architecture with the data protection officer
issues.body:
Schedule a meeting with the data protection officer (Datenschutzbeauftragter) to discuss the RAM-buffer architecture and clarify privacy requirements. (Was SCRUM-11 in Jira.)

**Done when**
- [ ] Meeting held, answers written down

issues.title: Consent form for test recordings
issues.body:
Form for students and lecturers before we record any audio for testing. Needed before the 5–6 h recordings can start.

**Done when**
- [ ] Form ready (Nextcloud or another local tool, not a US cloud form)

issues.title: Design the "Live-Untertitelung aktiv (KI)" sign
issues.body:
A sign for lecture halls and a banner in the viewer, so everyone knows live captioning is on.

**Done when**
- [ ] Printable sign in German and English

issues.title: Write the privacy notice text
issues.body:
Short text for the viewer: what we process, what we don't keep, who to contact. Only claims the backend can actually back up.

**Done when**
- [ ] Text agreed by backend and the privacy owner, used in the viewer

issues.title: Clarify whether the RAM buffer counts as recording (§201 StGB)
issues.body:
Lawyers disagree on whether live transcription with a short audio buffer counts as recording the spoken word. Ask the data protection officer.

**Done when**
- [ ] Answer written down in a decision record

epic.title: Epic 5: Translation & technical terms
epic.body:
**Goal:** Better accuracy on technical terms, and translation for students who don't follow German well.

**Note from the survey (N=13):** 85% need English captions, only 46% German, and 62% find German as a second language a barrier. Translation may need to move up from "later" — to discuss in sprint planning.

**Done when**
- [ ] Technical terms are pulled from lecture slides offline and passed to Whisper as hints
- [ ] We know which local translation model to use, with quality and delay measured

issues.title: Extract technical terms from lecture slides
issues.body:
Offline Python script (e.g. `pdfplumber` + `spaCy`) that pulls technical terms from a PDF and turns them into a hint list for Whisper.

**Done when**
- [ ] Works on a real lecture PDF without internet
- [ ] Output can be fed into the term hints test (Epic 1)

issues.title: Test local German → English translation
issues.body:
Compare local models (e.g. NLLB, MarianMT, or newer options) for translating live captions.

**Done when**
- [ ] Translation quality checked on our test text
- [ ] Extra delay per sentence measured
- [ ] Decision record on which model

issues.title: Check lectures that switch between German and English
issues.body:
Many IIS lectures are in English or mix both. Check how Whisper handles that (language detection vs fixed language).

**Done when**
- [ ] Test on a mixed German/English recording, result written down

epic.title: Epic 6: Speaker labels (Lecturer / Audience)
epic.body:
**Goal:** Show who is speaking (Lecturer vs Audience) **without** any biometric voice data, only by which microphone channel the audio comes from.

**Done when**
- [ ] The viewer shows two speakers with distinct colours **and** text labels
- [ ] Separation is based only on the hardware channel, no voice analysis

issues.title: Route two mic channels and tag captions with the channel
issues.body:
Channel 1: lecturer lav mic, channel 2: audience mic (e.g. Catchbox). Tag every caption with its channel ID and send it via WebSocket.

**Done when**
- [ ] Captions from each mic arrive with the right label
- [ ] One mic picking up the other doesn't create duplicate captions (tested)

issues.title: Show Lecturer / Audience in the viewer
issues.body:
Colour plus a text label like [Prof.] / [Frage], because colour alone isn't accessible.

**Done when**
- [ ] Labels readable on all themes and screen sizes
